CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidneys in patient with Smith-Magenis Syndrome.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Katherine is a 22-month-old female twin born at 34 weeks and 3 days gestation with birth weight of 4 pounds 8 ounces. She has an unaffected twin sister of similar size. She also has a 9-year-old brother with autism. 

Katherine had neonatal feeding difficulties with apneic episodes during eating and temperature regulation difficulties. She has been followed by a gastroenterologist for severe gastroesophageal reflux and was transitioned from cow's milk to ripple pea protein milk per dietician recommendation. She was diagnosed with Smith-Magenis Syndrome by a neurologist when she presented with developmental delay, specifically not sitting by herself at 1 year of age. She has since progressed and is now crawling and attempting to walk. She is currently in feeding therapy, occupational therapy, and physical therapy, with speech therapy starting within 2 weeks. She has also been evaluated by allergy, orthopedic, ophthalmology, and audiology. The family was counseled by genetics that Smith-Magenis Syndrome can be associated with kidney abnormalities, including possible kidney fusion. Parents report normal urination with 8-10 wet diapers per 24 hours and good fluid intake. Family resides in Dallas, Georgia.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient is asymptomatic. No urinary, kidney, or systemic symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Smith-Magenis Syndrome, prematurity at 34 weeks 3 days, neonatal low birth weight, neonatal feeding difficulties with apneic episodes, neonatal temperature regulation difficulties, gastroesophageal reflux disease, developmental delay.

MEDICATIONS
None reported.

ALLERGIES
Cow's milk intolerance.

FAMILY HISTORY
9-year-old brother with autism. Healthy twin sister. No family history of kidney disease, kidney failure, dialysis, or transplant.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives in Dallas, Georgia. Engaged in multiple therapy programs.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-nourished female, slightly fussy when examined. Eyes small appearing. Mild hypotonia of lower extremities and arms. Normal external female genitalia. Heart and lungs normal on auscultation. Ears examined without abnormality.

RESULTS
Kidney ultrasound ordered and pending.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
22-month-old female with Smith-Magenis Syndrome presenting for screening evaluation of kidneys given the reported association of this chromosomal deletion syndrome with congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract. Will obtain kidney ultrasound today. If normal, no further follow-up needed. If abnormal, will determine next steps and future follow-up at Town Center location. Will call family with results.
